sections.h2: Enlisted cell capacity has roughly tripled in fourteen months

chart.title: Cumulative enlisted capacity rose from 13,067 MW to 37,796 MW across 13 revisions
chart.sub: Cumulative enlisted cell capacity after each revision, MW a year.
chart.source: MNRE, ALMM List-II revisions 0-12; author's sums.

sections.means: The list grew in steps, with the biggest jump at the third revision on 15 December 2025.
sections.todo: Check the current List-II revision before ordering cells for any project that commissions after 31 December 2026.

sections.h2: Twelve company names hold 86% of enlisted capacity

chart.title: Waaree and TP Solar alone hold 26% of the list, and the top five names 52%
chart.sub: Share of total enlisted capacity by manufacturer, %.
chart.source: MNRE, ALMM List-II, 12th revision (8 October 2026); author's sums.

sections.means: Concentration is high, so a single plant's ramp-up or delay moves the national picture.
sections.todo: Ask suppliers which listed unit will make their cells and whether that unit is already at full output.

sections.h2: Gujarat and Tamil Nadu host most of the enlisted factories

chart.title: Gujarat holds 34% of enlisted capacity and Tamil Nadu 21%
chart.sub: Share of total enlisted capacity by state, %.
chart.source: MNRE, ALMM List-II, 12th revision (8 October 2026); author's sums.

sections.means: A developer in a state with no enlisted cell plant must buy from a neighbouring state.
sections.todo: Price cell sourcing from Gujarat, Tamil Nadu or Telangana before committing to a project site outside them.

sections.h2: Mono PERC still leads, but TOPCon is now 42% of the list

chart.title: Mono PERC is 46% of the list, TOPCon 42%, and the latest additions are TOPCon

sections.means: The list records manufacturer-claimed efficiency ranges, not tested values, so technology share is a capacity view only.
